prediction_ref.short_label: Multi-tenant agent builders draw a 9.0+ cross-tenant authz CVE by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The late-June CVE wave lands squarely on the multi-tenant agent-builder surface this prediction targets. Flowise MCP command-injection RCE headlines the cluster with CVE-2026-56274, a CVSS 9.9 OS-command-injection flaw in Flowise Custom MCP Server (before 3.1.2) where incomplete command-flag validation plus a regex bypass in local-file-access restrictions let any authenticated user configure a malicious MCP server that slips past the validateCommandFlags blocklist and runs arbitrary host commands. It sits inside a wider window: Crawl4AI (CVE-2026-53753), Langflow, and picklescan all scored 9.6-9.8, and Microsoft AutoGen Studio code execution traces to insufficient containerization so agent-generated code runs in the host process with excessive privileges. The exploit path is the authenticated-tenant-to-host escalation the prediction anticipates, and Flowise clears the 9.0+ threshold outright. The one gap versus the exact claim is that Flowise scopes on an authenticated user rather than an explicitly named cross-tenant authorization break, so the severity bar is met while the strict cross-tenant framing is only partially matched.

prediction_ref.short_label: Inline MCP-channel policy enforcement ships as a platform default by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today squarely names the MCP-server / tool-execution boundary as the concentrating point of exploitable code, which is precisely the channel this prediction says must gain inline default policy enforcement. Flowise custom-MCP command-injection RCE (CVE-2026-56274, CVSS 9.9) slips past a validateCommandFlags blocklist via a regex bypass to run arbitrary host commands, while Microsoft AutoGen Studio code execution runs agent-generated code in the host process with excessive privileges from insufficient containerization. The common thread the report draws is the plumbing that lets agents call tools being where the exploitable code sits. That is the demand-side pressure for inline MCP-channel enforcement, but no platform has yet shipped inline allowlist-based MCP policy as a shipped default; today is the incident evidence that motivates it, not the productized default itself.

prediction_ref.short_label: Coding-agent platform ships trifecta capability gate as default by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Two of today's signals touch the agent-harness reliability-and-authorization surface this prediction lives on. On the security side, the Flowise custom-MCP RCE (CVE-2026-56274) and the AutoGen Studio host-process code execution both come from a trust-the-authenticated-user, run-on-the-host pattern that a deny-by-default capability gate is designed to foreclose. On the model side, Anthropic ships Claude Sonnet 5 flagging a lower rate of undesirable behaviors and better resistance to prompt-injection hijack attempts than its predecessor. But neither is the load-bearing mechanism: a default-on gate capping the lethal trifecta of private-data access, untrusted content, and external communication. Model-level injection resistance and framework RCE disclosures raise the pressure for such a gate without any coding-agent platform shipping the deny-by-default authorization control itself, so the relevance is thematic rather than direct fulfillment.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agent-framework SQL tools ship read-only-by-default execution guards by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: [REVIVED] The late-June agent-tooling CVE cluster re-anchors the execution-layer-guard thesis. Flowise custom-MCP command-injection (CVE-2026-56274, CVSS 9.9) runs arbitrary host commands because incomplete flag validation and a regex bypass defeat a blocklist, and AutoGen Studio executes agent-generated code in the host process with excessive privileges from insufficient containerization. Both are the same prompt-to-tool-to-execution abuse that read-only-by-default, least-privilege execution guards are meant to blunt, and blocklist-defeated-by-bypass is exactly the failure mode the prediction argues pushes frameworks toward allowlist, least-privilege defaults. The evidence is the injection-class incident pressure rather than a shipped read-only-by-default SQL or execution guard in a named framework, so it revives the dormant thesis without fulfilling it.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agentic coding platforms ship token budgets and caps as default by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5 on June 30 as the cheapest way to run long-horizon agents at close to flagship quality, claiming cost-performance parity with Opus 4.8 on the BrowseComp agentic-search and OSWorld-Verified computer-use benchmarks at introductory $2 per million input / $10 per million output tokens (standard $3/$15 after August 31), and shipping as the default on Free and Pro. Driving per-token cost for capable agentic loops to roughly a third of flagship is the same enterprise-token-bill pressure that motivates platforms to expose budgets and caps by default: cheaper tokens do not remove the need to bound long-horizon agent spend, they raise the volume of autonomous loops running. This is substrate-cost context that sharpens the economic case for default budgets rather than a platform shipping the token-cap control itself.

prediction_ref.short_label: Orchestration benchmarks add a latency-disclosure column by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 29 arXiv batch pushes agent orchestration to the front of the research agenda: Design and Implementation of Agentic Orchestrations and Orchestration of Agents (2606.31518) treats how agents are composed and orchestrated as the first-order engineering concern rather than an afterthought, alongside a self-evolving biological-protocol agent (2606.31763) and a plant-phenotyping framework, converging on orchestration and self-evolving autonomy in domain-specific settings. Elevating orchestration to a first-class engineering object is the precondition for orchestration-specific benchmarks and the disclosure columns this prediction expects, but the papers frame composition and self-evolution rather than standardized latency reporting, so the evidence advances the orchestration-benchmark direction without adding the specific latency-disclosure column.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agent meta-harness becomes the cross-vendor policy plane for agents by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Anthropic Claude Science launched June 30 as a harness rather than a new model: it runs the existing Claude models (including Opus 4.8, no special access) and adds pre-configured connectors to more than 60 scientific databases and computation tools across genomics, proteomics, structural biology and cheminformatics, with the differentiated product being the tool-integration and domain-skills layer around a general model, not the weights. Paired with the June 29 orchestration arXiv work (2606.31518) treating composition and orchestration as the first-order concern, the signal reinforces that the harness and policy-and-integration layer over models is where competitive value is moving. It is directional support for a harness becoming the durable control surface, but Claude Science is a single-vendor domain workbench, not a cross-vendor policy plane spanning multiple labs' models, which is the specific claim.
